newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up, led by Refrigerator.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up, led by Refrigerator.

text.p: Shanghai B shares reversed morning losses to end up on Thursday, led by gains in Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor which boosted buying interest in blue-chips, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.610 points or 0.71 percent to 86.958 points on volume of 39.816 million shares worth $23.245 million, compared with $17.129 million on Wednesday.
The B index met strong support at 85 points following morning losses and later rose on institutional buying in Shanghai Refrigerator, which stimulated buying interest in blue-chips, brokers said.

Official financial newspapers reported on Thursday that the China Securities Regulatory Commission would focus its 1997 work on strengthening market supervision and standardising market activity in a drive to improve risk control.
The news caused B share losses in the morning which were later offset by gains in blue-chips, led by Shanghai Refrigerator, in the afternoon, brokers said.
Shanghai Refrigerator was the most actively traded and become the second biggest gainer, ending at a historical high by jumping $0.048 or 7.16 percent to $0.718 on volume of 3.5 million shares.
"Blue chip Shanghai Refrigerator offered a good bonus issue, which was attractive to investors," said one broker.

The company's board of directors has proposed a three-for-10 bonus issue and a three-for-10 rights issue, pending approval at a shareholders meeting scheduled for May 30, the company said in a statement on Thursday.

"The market is likely to consolidate around current levels in the short term due to uncertainties over unpublished 1996 results and Beijing's further measures to cool down the market," another broker said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 21 up and 22 down.
Another blue chip, Shanghai Chlor Alkai, was the star on institutional buying, surging $0.144 or 9.95 percent to $1.590 on volume of 405,600 shares.
Shanghai's A share index edged up on institutional buying in selected stocks late in the session, but most investors were cautious, brokers said.
The index inched up 1.279 points or 0.09 percent to 1,443.897 points on volume of 933.0 million shares worth 13.0 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 45.458 points or 1.21 percent to 3,792.197 points.
Jiangxi Paper was the best A share performer on speculative buying, soaring 1.69 yuan or 10.02 percent to 18.54 yuan on volume of 8.1 million shares.
